If God loves us, if there's a divine spark in us, then we should know what is right and what is wrong. The first and most important thing he does is propose an egalitarian society where men and women are equal with no hierarchy and rabbis are not above you because the law doesn't exist anymore; what matters is your relationship to God. In many ways, he's a proto-liberal and a protocommunist. He believes that in the system designed as it is, you must obey the rabbi and await the coming of Messiah who will take us back to Jerusalem.

It's meant to defend the status quo and make Jews slaves to the nobility. He's very much a pro-egalitarian and pro-communist; we'll discuss his influence on modernity next class. The first thing I want you to remember is that he ultimately converts to Islam. When he announced himself as Messiah, a million Jews follow him because he preaches liberation, equality, and freedom. But when confronted by the Sultan, the Sultan says the turban or your head; converting means redemption for all Jews from the original sin of conversion.

So, Zabdi Zevi sacrifices himself to redeem the Jews, absolving them of the original sin with God, allowing you to be close with God and no longer follow laws. The messianic age has come because you are the messianic age now. He suggests justification by faith, not breaking laws. In fact, he converts to Islam, eats pork, and engages in various activities, breaking many laws. But what Zevi means is that in this new age, laws don't apply; breaking them shows true faith in God.

Most Jews choose to follow the rabbis, but 300 families convert with him, forming the Doma, eventually controlling Turkey. Fifty years after his death, Jacob Frank emerges as a reincarnation of Zabdi Zevi and follows his teachings.
